h: The Kohanim Sanctify Shabbos by Teaching Lasting Torah

p: We read as the haftarah "And the Kohanim, the Levi'im" (Yechezkel 44:15),
which speaks of the holiness of the Kohanim;
"And My people they shall teach, etc." (Yechezkel 44:23),
in the manner of what it says (Devarim 33:10),
"They shall teach Your judgments to Yaakov, etc.";
in all My festivals they shall keep,
and My Shabbosos they shall sanctify."
what does it have to do with the holiness of the Kohanim,
when this applies to all of Yisrael?
Also the word "they shall sanctify" is hard to understand,
and "My Shabbosos they shall keep" would have fit.
that it refers to the obligation of the offerings,
the word "they shall sanctify" needs explanation,
on the contrary, Shabbos sanctifies the offerings,
for the temidin and the mussafin of Shabbos are called
on the reason why that of Rosh Chodesh is called
because it is called a festival.
And we have already said the meaning:
and from the side of Yisrael it is holier
But why did Rashi not explain
on the grounds that the offerings of Rosh Chodesh
are more than those of Shabbos?
such that more offerings would mean greater stature;
and if so, the expression is not understood,
And if it refers to the holiness of Shabbos in general,
in the manner of what they said in the Mechilta
"'And on the seventh day you shall rest'
לֹא תֵּעָקֵר שַׁבַּת בְּרֵאשִׁית מִמְּקוֹמָהּ וְכוּלֵּי
the Shabbos of Creation shall not be uprooted from its place, etc."
That is: the whole point of Shabbos
is that they be free for Torah and avodah,
and in Shemittah, all year long
since their main labor was in the field,
and one might have thought they are exempt from Shabbos
And likewise one might have thought regarding the Kohanim,
whose livelihood is from the priestly gifts,
who have no portion or inheritance in the land
that they would be exempt from Shabbos
the word "they shall sanctify" is still not resolved,
and "they shall keep" would have fit better.
כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר וְאֶת עַמִּי יוֹרוּ וְגוֹ׳
as it says, "And My people they shall teach, etc.":
and were the teachers of Yisrael;
to see to it that there be fixed
the words of Torah in the heart of Yisrael;
through the holiness of festival and Shabbos,
at the conclusion of Shabbosos and Yamim Tovim:
"You have graced us with knowledge of Your Torah."
That is, on Shabbosos and Yamim Tovim,
for Shabbosos and Yamim Tovim were given
only to occupy oneself in them with words of Torah
and then they merit the aspect of daas,
שֶׁבָּא עַל יְדֵי חִיבּוּר חָכְמָה וּבִינָה
which comes through the union of Chochmah and Binah,
"And teach us to perform the statutes of Your will":
that it be engraved in the heart
doers of the will of the Omnipresent.
in all My festivals they shall keep,"
in the manner of what is said in the Mechilta,
that the words of Torah be engraved in the heart
and they merit the aspect of daas;
"For the lips of a Kohen shall keep knowledge"
And then "Torah they shall seek from his mouth":
that the words of Torah be fixed
that they merit the Shabbosos of Hashem,
regarding what is said in the Gemara (Shabbos 118b),
אִיתָא שֶׁעַל יְדֵי שְׁמִירַת שַׁבָּת אַחַת
it states that through keeping one Shabbos
And we said that the meaning is:
when one merits the holiness of the supernal Shabbos,
And one who merits this with one Shabbos
but for the most part this requires
the holiness of the workdays helps
that one merit the aspect of the supernal Shabbos
that an am ha'aretz merits on Shabbos
חֵלֶק ג קכד, סוֹף עַמּוּד ב)
which are the two Shabbosos of Hashem.
"And Bnei Yisrael shall keep the Shabbos":
to instill holiness into the six workdays;
as is written in the Tikkunei Zohar
"And the yetzer hara is cleared out of there."
And about this the pasuk said
who are always free for Torah
into the Shabbosos of all Yisrael;
for through the holiness of the Kohanim
being free in the six workdays
they merit and bring merit to all Yisrael,
to make a dwelling for them
in the two chambers of the heart,
"and the yetzer hara is cleared out of there."
